skill.name: lark-doc
skill.description: Use authenticated lark-cli commands to read, create, update, and manage Lark Docs or Feishu Wiki documents from AI assistants.
skill.summary: Read, create, update, and manage Lark Docs content, media, history, and word counts through lark-cli.
skill.author: larksuite

security_audit.summary: The static findings are caused by markdown examples, placeholder URLs, inline code fences, readable Chinese documentation, and a local word-count parser. No prompt injection text, hidden payload, or malicious command construction was found in the reviewed files. The skill still performs authenticated Lark document reads and writes, so users should confirm destructive or data-exporting actions.

remediation.issue: Relative links reference sibling Lark skills outside this package.
remediation.suggestion: Declare shared Lark skill dependencies explicitly or vendor required safety guidance into this package.

remediation.issue: Document update, media, and history operations can change or export user data.
remediation.suggestion: Keep explicit confirmation before writes, deletes, media downloads, cover changes, and history reverts.

remediation.issue: Some shell examples include quoting and command substitution patterns.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer file or stdin examples for multiline content and label shell snippets as illustrative examples.

content.user_title: Manage Lark Docs from AI Assistants
content.value_statement: Teams often need document changes without switching between tools. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through authenticated lark-cli workflows for Lark Docs.
actual_capabilities: Fetch Lark Docx or Wiki content by URL or token with XML, Markdown, scope, and detail options.
Create new Lark documents from XML or Markdown content.
Update documents with append, overwrite, text replacement, block insertion, block replacement, deletion, move, and copy operations.
Insert, preview, download, update, or delete document media and cover resources.
Inspect document history, revert to a selected version, and calculate word or character counts with the included script.
limitations: Requires lark-cli, an authenticated Lark account, and permissions for the target document.
Does not manage document comments or cloud drive permissions directly.
Embedded sheets, Base apps, notes, and whiteboards require separate Lark skills for internal object operations.
Media insertion from the clipboard depends on platform clipboard support and local helper tools on Linux.

use_cases.title: Summarize a Lark Doc Section
use_cases.description: Fetch only the needed section, preserve block context, and produce a focused summary for a stakeholder.

use_cases.title: Publish a Team Document
use_cases.description: Create a structured Lark document from a brief, then refine sections and insert approved media.

use_cases.title: Maintain Existing Documentation
use_cases.description: Locate target blocks, apply precise edits, keep embedded resources intact, and verify the updated content.

prompt_templates.title: Read a Document
prompt_templates.prompt: Read this Lark document and summarize the main points. Use the smallest useful fetch scope when possible: [document URL].

prompt_templates.title: Create a New Document
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Lark document for this topic. Use clear headings, concise paragraphs, and confirm the resulting document link: [topic and requirements].

prompt_templates.title: Edit a Specific Section
prompt_templates.prompt: Update only the section named [section name] in this Lark document. Preserve existing mentions, media, sheets, and resource tokens: [document URL].

prompt_templates.title: Refine and Verify a Long Document
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve this long Lark document for [audience]. Fetch the outline first, edit sections sequentially, verify the result, and run word-count validation if a target length is provided: [document URL].

output_examples.input: Summarize the launch plan section from a Lark document.
output_examples.output: A concise section summary with the launch goals, timeline, owners, and unresolved decisions.

output_examples.input: Create a project FAQ in Lark Docs from a short brief.
output_examples.output: A new document link with a title, grouped questions, direct answers, and a short next-steps section.

output_examples.input: Rewrite one section and keep existing media references.
output_examples.output: A confirmation that only the requested section changed, with embedded images and linked resources preserved.

best_practices: Confirm user intent before any write, delete, media download, or history revert operation.
Fetch outlines or sections before large documents to reduce unnecessary data access.
Preserve resource tokens, mentions, embedded sheets, and media unless the user explicitly asks to change them.
anti_patterns: Do not fetch an entire document when a section, keyword, or range fetch is enough.
Do not overwrite a document when the user requested a precise section edit.
Do not guess local file paths or clipboard content when inserting media.

faq.question: Does this skill require Lark authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It depends on lark-cli and the permissions of the authenticated user account.

faq.question: Can it edit an existing Lark document?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports text replacement, block operations, append, overwrite, and media insertion workflows.

faq.question: Can it work with Feishu Wiki links?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill supports Docx and Wiki document URLs or tokens when lark-cli can resolve them.

faq.question: Does it manage comments?
faq.answer: No. Comment workflows are outside this skill and should use the related Lark Drive skill.

faq.question: Can it read embedded sheets or Base tables?
faq.answer: It can detect their tokens, but internal sheet or Base data operations require the corresponding Lark skill.

faq.question: Is media download automatic?
faq.answer: No. Media download should only happen when the user clearly asks for the asset or preview.
